tier0.label: Business critical
tier0.note: Loss of this asset or identity degrades the whole environment, not one user.

entries.name: domain_controllers
entries.note: Isolation severs Kerberos and LDAP for every host that authenticates here, so the blast radius of the response exceeds the incident.

entries.name: certificate_authority
entries.note: Certificate issuance and revocation checking stop environment-wide.

entries.name: virtualization_hosts
entries.note: Contains every guest on the host, most of which are unrelated to the incident.

entries.name: security_tooling
entries.note: Responding on the response infrastructure removes the ability to respond to anything else.

entries.name: production_databases
entries.note: Recoverable but customer-visible. A human confirms the outage is worth it.

entries.name: break_glass_accounts
entries.note: These are the credentials used to recover from a bad response, so they must survive one.

entries.name: service_accounts
entries.note: One service account often backs several applications, and the dependency list is rarely written down.

entries.name: privileged_identities
entries.note: Disabling the account an incident responder is using to respond is a self-inflicted outage.
